verdict: Not exit-ready: 3 BLOCKER (all three are the red validator), 3 MAJOR, 10 MINOR. The unit has a good story spine. The lost Heft from u05's cliffhanger turns up in Herr Richter's lost-and-found, Arta joins online and asks what her key is called, and Bilal hunts a used laptop, so the scenes carry the grammar. The German is correct on every model surface, and du/Sie is right everywhere (the course duzt, Frau Schulz and Herr Richter siezen, and Nora even states the rule). The dictations match their audio, the typed numbers accept their words, and the sentence-building prompts name Aussagesatz/Frage, so most u04 classes stayed closed. L2, Sp2, Sp3 and S2 match sd1.json in items, options, cards, modes and Leitpunkte. Several classes are back, however. (1) All seven error corrections have the bare „Korrigieren Sie:“ prompt, the u04 r5-F01 class that the exemplar ended on. The rail for it now exists and fails the unit, and in at least five items a correct correction is graded WRONG („Frau Schulz sucht die Schlüssel.“, „Ich habe keine Laptops.“). (2) The same blind spot hits three fill-blanks: the cues (mein)/(kein) before Schlüssel and Drucker, whose plural is identical, admit „meine/keine“, and the grader rejects them. (3) LS2's structured-input item puts Bilal's line into Herr Richter's mouth and explains „keinen Drucker“ in a way that Richter's own line contradicts. (4) cd.a1.wort-fehlt is proven only by a recognition item with implausible distractors; the circumlocution it names is never produced (the u04 r1-F07/F13 and u05 r1-F03 class). The other red rules: LEX-01 finds „Situationen“ and „Geschafft“ again (u05 r1-F01's words) and a title.canDo with „kurze“ and „passender“, and GRM-05 finds that rc.akkusativ ignores the unit's own dative chunk. The minors recur from u05 r1: word-spotting L2 items, short ads, look-aheads on unread surfaces, and production on receptive lemmas. There is one new story break: Priya's husband is a software developer, yet the laptop plot never mentions him.

findings.quote: ls3-p04 „Ich suche ___ Schlüssel. (mein)“ → only „meinen“ · ls3-r04 „Hast du ___ Schlüssel? (mein)“ → only „meinen“ · ls2-p03 „Heute haben wir ___ Drucker. (kein)“ → only „keinen“ · promptEn „mein → accusative form.“ / „kein → form for der Drucker.“ · lexicon plural: lx.schluessel „Schlüssel“, lx.drucker „Drucker“ · ls1-l10 „der Schlüssel, die Schlüssel“
findings.problem: Schlüssel and Drucker have one form for singular and plural, and the cues „(mein)“ and „(kein)“ are the base of both the masculine singular and the plural. „Ich suche meine Schlüssel.“ and „Hast du meine Schlüssel?“ are not only correct; they are what Germans say about their keys, and LS1 has just taught „die Schlüssel“. „Heute haben wir keine Drucker.“ is correct too. Only ls2-p03's promptEn („form for der Drucker“) fixes the number, and ITM-01 forbids a cue that sits only in the English. The grader marks „meine“ and „keine“ WRONG, so a learner who reads the German correctly is told they made a case error, and the case-np repair card then drills a rule they did not break. Five of the unit's 24 nouns have an identical plural (Schlüssel, Drucker, Computer, Kalender, Ladekabel), so the class will recur wherever kein/mein cues meet them. The other items are safe only by accident, because „(der)“ and „(ein)“ fix the number (ls1-p04, c01, ls3-r01).
findings.fix: Use nouns whose plural differs. ls3-p04: „Ich suche ___ Kuli. (mein)“ → „meinen“, explanation „der Kuli → einen Kuli → meinen Kuli“. ls3-r04: „Hast du ___ Laptop? (mein)“ → „meinen“. ls2-p03: „Heute hat Olena ___ Kuli. (kein)“ → „keinen“ (F05 changes the input sentence it copied). The alternative is to put the number into the German cue („(mein, Singular)“), which is clumsier.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-01: a fill_blank whose German cue is a determiner base that has a plural form (kein, mein, dein, Ihr, sein, ihr, unser, euer) and whose blank precedes a noun whose lexicon `plural` equals its lemma must carry a German number cue or accept the plural determiner with acceptedWhy. An error_correction whose planted error is the definite article of such a noun must accept the plural article. Failing fixtures: a1.1-u06 ls3-p04, ls3-r04, ls2-p03, ls1-r04. Passing: ls1-p04 („(der)“), c01 („(ein)“). The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.problem: The can-do's defining half is the repair: showing or describing the thing whose word is missing („Das ist für mein Handy“). No task in the unit asks the learner to produce it. ls1-mo prints „Wie heißt das auf Deutsch?“ in the prompt and asks for nothing more, and neither Sprechen part has a moment where a word is missing. The only proof is a recognition item. Its two distractors ask for a price and an age, so the key is the only option that asks for a name at all, and no option tempts the typical failure (using the word one does not know, or giving up). The can-do is therefore claimed rather than performed. This is the u04 r1-F07/F13 and u05 r1-F03 class (MAJOR), and the validator's ALL-02 advisory points at it. The Sp3 format supplies the authentic occasion: in the exam the cards are pictures, and a candidate who does not know the word must describe the object.

exitCheck.note: Exit needs 0 BLOCKER, 0 MAJOR, every criterion ≥ 4 and ≤ 5 logged MINOR. The unit author can close F01 and F02 (turning ITM-01 and LEX-01 green) and all three MAJORs (F04, F05, F06) with data edits in u06.json. The same holds for the unit parts of F07–F16. F03 (GRM-05) is owned by the rule-cards file and the spine label, and the unit cannot exit until it is green. Owner work: rule-cards F03; spine F03 (label) and F11 (g.praep-akkusativ chunkFrom); lexicon F12 (promotions); level reviewer F12 (LEX-02 routing); SCHEMA F13 (castIn); rule-smith F02 (metalanguage decision owed since u05 r1-F01; „Geschafft“ now fails in ten units), F04, F06, F07, F08, F09, F10, F11 and F12. After the unit edits, the expected residue is 2–3 owner-held minors (F11's spine part, F12's lexicon part, F13's SCHEMA part), which is within the limit. u04 finding classes that recur here: r5-F01 (bare error corrections, now a rail), r1-F07/F13 (can-do claimed), r2-F02 (mirror order), r2-F08 (Sp2 chip not logged), r4-F02 (production on receptive lemmas), r4-F08 (article-less adjective on a strategy card), r1-F10 (short exam texts), r1-F19/r1-F20 (word-spotting, repeated scene). u04 classes that stayed closed: dictation vs audio, number words in typed numbers, Frage/Satz in sentence-building prompts, genitive in speaking instructions, rule card case labels, key position (the player shuffles), H1 facts vs the story, and the price arithmetic.
